Root194 equation (6), and the corresponding printed BJ v4 equation (3.22) with that factor order, have reversed coefficients. On the blowup of P²×P¹ at (p,0), the model H−aE gives J=a³/3 whereas the supplied formula gives 2a³/3. Corrected positive weights remain between 1 and n, so the raw Hölder moment estimate with exponent 2^−n follows from the finite Hodge argument with dimension-only constants, including A^n=0. notes.text:
Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued, of characteristic zero; let Z be smooth integral projective of dimension n≥1, A an actual nef rational bundle, and h, ψ bounded relatively nef model scalars on A. All models and rational divisors are actual, and rational coefficients are cleared. Write T_ξ=(A,ξ), e_A(ξ)=T_ξ^(n+1)/(n+1), V_A=A^n≥0, μ_A(ξ) for the raw finite model measure, and J_A(ξ)=ξ(v0)V_A−e_A(ξ). Central measure coefficients retain b_E(T_ξ|E)^n. There is no volume denominator.

The correct algebraic identity, for S=T_ξ−T_η=(0,ξ−η), is
T_η^(n+1)−T_ξ^(n+1)+(n+1)S T_η^n = −Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}(n−j) S² T_ξ^j T_η^(n−1−j).
Indeed telescope the difference of (n+1)st powers. After subtracting its linear term, telescope each T_ξ^k T_η^(n−k)−T_η^n. The term indexed by j occurs for k=j+1,…,n, exactly n−j times. Since (0,ξ)T_0^n=ξ(v0)V_A, this gives
J_A(ξ)=(n+1)^−1 Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}(n−j) ||ξ||²_{T_ξ^j T_0^(n−1−j)},
where ||f||²_{T_1…T_(n−1)}=−(0,f)²T_1…T_(n−1). These seminorms are nonnegative by the finite vertical Hodge inequality. Swapping to coefficients j+1 requires swapping the order of the two families of factors as well.

This discrepancy is realized by a genuine model in the actual ample G0 domain. On Y=Bl_(p,0)(P²×P¹), let H be the pulled hyperplane, E the exceptional divisor, and 0<a<1 rational. H−aE is relatively ample: its restrictions on the two central components are H−aE_p on Bl_p P² and O_P²(a), respectively. E≅P², E|E=O(−1), and H|E is trivial. Thus H³=H²E=HE²=0 and E³=1. The scalar ξ of −aE has generic value zero, e_A(ξ)=−a³/3, ||ξ||²_T0=0 and ||ξ||²_Tξ=a³. Consequently J_A(ξ)=a³/3; the supplied j+1 formula gives 2a³/3. Its raw measure is (1−a²)δ_v0+a²δ_vE, with central multiplicities one. For a=1/2 the true cost is 1/24, the incorrect cost is 1/12, and the integral of ξ is −1/8. This is a mathematical counterexample to that identity, not to P16.5.

The uniform finite-nef moment estimate remains valid with corrected comparability:
∫(h(v0)−h)dμ_A(ψ) ≤ C_n J_A(h)^α J_A(ψ)^(1/2) max(J_A(h),J_A(ψ))^(1/2−α), α=2^−n.
Here C_n depends only on dimension. To check the estimate, define d_A(ξ,η) as the maximum of the n seminorm squares with factors T_ξ^j T_η^(n−1−j). The corrected tangent remainder has positive weights 1,…,n and is comparable to d_A; it is convex in its first potential by finite nef energy concavity. Expanding at the average τ=(ξ+ξ′)/2 gives ||ξ−ξ′||²_Tτ^(n−1) comparable to d_A(ξ,ξ′). Put b_j=||ξ−ξ′||²_(T_η^j T_τ^(n−1−j)), a=d_A(ξ,ξ′), b=max(d_A(ξ,η),d_A(ξ′,η)). Splitting a changed slot into the ξ and ξ′ slots and applying Cauchy–Schwarz yields b_(j+1)−b_j≤C_n√(b b_j), with b_0≤C_na and b_(n−1)≤4b. Induction gives the final-slot exponent 2^(1−n). Splitting differences through a third potential and absorbing the larger side proves the quasi-triangle bound. Expansion of an average of mixed nef slots gives the same bound for mixed seminorms. Now shift h and ψ to generic value zero, and telescope μ_A(ψ)−μ_A(0) from j=0 through n−1. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to each term; the h factor supplies exponent 2^−n and the ψ factor supplies 1/2. Corrected J comparability gives the displayed estimate. For n=1 use the literal empty product seminorm. Zero seminorm cases follow directly; exponent-zero factors are interpreted by continuity. When V_A=0, positivity and zero mass force μ_A(ψ)=0 without probability normalization.

The finite Hodge inequality and ordinary intersection background are explicitly separate from caller grants. G0 is used only on actual ample models or for fixed-model finite polynomial perturbations. No general nef or big unbounded equation is inferred. The printed BJ v4 factor order was checked at original renderer lines 2893–2910 and PDF page index 42, printed page 43. Its finite slot-replacement proof was read in complete pertinent units. All broader Complete151 conclusions remain unreviewed conditions where used.

notes.summary: Proved an arbitrary-support compact-Hausdorff Radon-net squeeze with explicit envelope-discrepancy errors. Zero discrepancies imply fixed original continuous L1 approximants for bounded relative tests. General big-output discrepancy nullness remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: For positive weakly converging Radon nets, uniformly bounded changing tests squeezed locally between fixed lsc/usc bounds have limiting integral bounds given by the endpoint bounds on the entire limiting support, provided increasing good opens carry full limiting mass. Applied to complete section quotients, the errors are ∫min(2C,u_H−Q_H) and ∫min(2C,Vθ−Q_0). If both discrepancies vanish almost everywhere, a fixed continuous test on the original compact carrier approximates both the limiting relative quotient and the changing quotients in absolute L1, with collar and fixed degree selected before the measure limit. This result has no atomicity or metrizability assumption. A nonatomic square example shows why bounded moments, weak convergence and increasing continuous section-like stages alone cannot remove the discrepancies. The NA application remains conditional on genuine envelopes and output foundations; it supplies no unbounded tail theorem.
notes.text:
Here is a purely measure-theoretic theorem, proved without using any nonample equation theorem. Let K be compact Hausdorff, ν_i positive Radon measures converging weakly to ν with converging finite masses, and a_i measurable on their supports with |a_i|≤C. Let U_q be increasing open sets whose union G has full ν mass. On U_q let ℓ_q,r_q∈[−C,C] be respectively lsc and usc, and suppose ℓ_q≤a_i≤r_q on the measure supports in U_q eventually for every fixed q. Let a∈[−C,C] be Borel on G, with ℓ_q≤a≤r_q and pointwise limiting bounds ℓ_∞,r_∞. Then
∫ℓ_∞dν ≤ liminf_i∫a_i dν_i ≤ limsup_i∫a_i dν_i ≤ ∫r_∞dν.
No support, countability or metrizability condition is imposed on ν.

Proof: bounded lsc tests have the weak lower integral inequality for Radon nets on compact Hausdorff spaces. They are directed suprema of continuous minorants, and Radon inner regularity plus continuous cutoffs approximates their integrals from below. Negation gives the upper inequality for bounded usc tests. For fixed q choose compact F_q⊂U_q with ν(U_q\F_q)<1/q and a continuous cutoff χ_q equal to one on F_q and supported in U_q. The products χ_qℓ_q and χ_qr_q extend by zero to bounded lsc/usc functions on K: at the collar boundary their absolute values are at most Cχ_q→0. Apply the two weak integral inequalities. The discarded part is at most C(ν_i(K)−∫χ_qdν_i). First take the measure-net limit with q and collar fixed, then q→∞. Since ν(G)=ν(K), the collar error tends to zero; bounded convergence gives the theorem.

If ℓ_∞=a=r_∞ almost everywhere, there is also an absolute L1 approximation statement. For every ε>0 choose b∈C(K), |b|≤C, such that ∫|a−b|dν<ε and eventually ∫|a_i−b|dν_i<ε. Continuous L1 approximation of bounded Borel functions follows from Radon regularity, simple functions and compact/open cutoffs. For a fixed q and collar, R_(q,b)=χ_q max(r_q−b,b−ℓ_q,0), extended by zero, is bounded usc and majorizes χ_q|a_i−b|. Its limiting integral is at most ∫|a−b|dν+∫_(U_q)(r_q−ℓ_q)dν. The omitted error is at most 2C(ν(K)−∫χ_qdν). Select q, collar and b with these errors small before taking i to its limit. This proves simultaneous actual continuous approximants, without uniform convergence of the changing tests.

Conditional original-carrier section application: assume genuine model envelopes u_H=Pθ(f_H), Vθ=Pθ(0), and full increasing degree-divisibility stages φ_(q,H)≤u_H, φ_(q,0)≤Vθ. Their actual time lattices give |φ_(q,H)−φ_(q,0)|≤C wherever finite; envelope monotonicity gives |u_H−Vθ|≤C off reference poles. Take a factorial sequence of nonempty degrees. On U_q where both fixed stages are finite, put ℓ_q=max(−C,φ_(q,H)−Vθ) and r_q=min(C,u_H−φ_(q,0)). These have the required lsc/usc signs and bound the changing quotient a_m=φ_(m,H)−φ_(m,0) for sufficiently divisible m. On actual pushed auxiliary divisorial atoms the shared horizontal-factor identity identifies this quotient with ψ_(m,H), with no infinity subtraction. Let Q_H=sup_qφ_(q,H), Q_0=sup_qφ_(q,0), a=u_H−Vθ, Δ_H=u_H−Q_H and Δ_0=Vθ−Q_0. Assuming full limiting mass on G, the theorem gives
∫a dν−∫min(2C,Δ_H)dν ≤ liminf_m∫a_m dν_m,
limsup_m∫a_m dν_m ≤ ∫a dν+∫min(2C,Δ_0)dν.
Thus zero output discrepancy gives the general weighted identity and continuous approximants for the bounded relative quotient. It does not show absolute integrability of Vθ or u_H, and does not establish uniform tails for unbounded E1 tests. Genuine envelope membership, the section-stage supremum interpretation, the original output measure and its good-locus mass are explicit conditions, not grants from historical papers.

The missing discrepancy is substantive even with bounded tests. On [0,1]² set φ_q(x,y)=min(1,qx), let ν_m be Lebesgue mass one along x=1/m², and let ν be Lebesgue mass one along x=0. Uniform continuity of each fixed continuous test proves ν_m→ν. The stages increase to Q=1 for x>0 and Q=0 for x=0; its usc regularization is u=1 everywhere. Nevertheless ∫φ_m dν_m=1/m→0 while ∫u dν=1. Every test is bounded by one, and the limiting measure is nonatomic. The discrepancy u−Q is one on its entire support. This is a mathematical compact-space diagnostic, not a claimed NA counterexample.

notes.text:
Let ν_i→ν be positive Radon measures on compact Hausdorff K. Let φ_q be increasing extended-continuous section-like functions, finite on increasing open U_q, and φ_q≤V*. Put G=∪U_q, Q*=sup_qφ_q, and assume ν(G)=ν(K) and V* finite on G. Let v be an actual usc function with v≤V*, and suppose the actual relative gaps are defined on the measure supports and ∫(V*−v)dν_i≤A(v)<∞ for all i. Then
∫_G(Q*−v)_+dν≤A(v).
If Rν=∫_G(V*−Q*)dν<∞, also
∫(V*−v)dν≤A(v)+Rν.
This is a conditional implication in measure theory, valid for every test satisfying its stated moment hypothesis; it is not an assertion that general big-class outputs satisfy the reference-defect condition.

Proof: fix q first. On U_q, b_q=(φ_q−v)_+ is nonnegative lsc, possibly infinite, because φ_q is finite continuous there and −v is lsc. For a continuous 0≤χ≤1 supported inside U_q, extend χ min(N,b_q) by zero. It is bounded lsc on K; nonnegativity gives the lower boundary inequality. On every measure support it is at most V*−v. The Radon-net semicontinuity proved in n2 bounds its ν integral by A(v). Let N→∞, then exhaust U_q in integral by compact sets and fixed continuous cutoffs. This gives ∫_(U_q)b_q dν≤A(v). Extended by zero these nonnegative functions increase with q, so monotone convergence gives the first assertion. On G, Q* is finite wherever V* is finite, since some stage is finite; finite Rν additionally controls any extended defect exceptions. The pointwise inequality 0≤V*−v≤(Q*−v)_++(V*−Q*) gives the second assertion, including infinite test values.

The intended full big rational-bundle application retains every smooth projective X and every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field. It assumes, rather than grants, the genuine closure, minimal reference, nonpositive cofinal model-envelope approximation, actual section-volume energy and target-independent weak output foundations from Complete151. It also assumes the actual common horizontal section factorizations, their generic-value and energy limits, and full limiting mass on the algebraic good locus. Under these exact conditions the finite model result n1, simultaneous complete-moving cofinality, and n2's finite-divisorial application yield for each fixed model output of cost ≤B:
∫(Vθ−v)dν_i≤A(v)=C_n B(v)^α B^(1/2) max(B(v),B)^(1/2−α), α=2^−n,
for every normalized genuine v∈E1. To pass the test to v, first decrease nonpositive original model obstacles majorizing v. Their envelopes have generic value zero, since they dominate v and lie below zero. Their energies decrease to E(v). Monotone integration at the fixed finite output support passes the moment estimate to v. No subtraction of varying generic constants is used to manufacture a decreasing net. The finite-nef generic error and moving volume limit are taken before this genuine test limit.

For a general weak output M(u), the transfer therefore controls the Q0-based gap. The missing extra term is precisely R_(M(u))=∫(Vθ−Q0)dM(u). Algebraic section-zero nullness, even if the proposed Complete151 proof is verified, can give full mass on G but does not control this defect inside G. Neither finiteness nor vanishing of R_(M(u)) is proved here. Thus the note does not claim unconditioned integrability of every E1 test against every big output.

There is also no uniform-tail or strong fixed-target integration theorem in this conclusion. An elementary diagnostic is ν_m=m^−1δ_(1/m)+(1−m^−1)δ_1 on [0,1], w(x)=1/x for x>0 and w(0)=∞. Then ν_m→δ_1, ∫w dν_m=2−1/m≤2 while the limiting integral is one. For any fixed truncation level N>1, ∫_{w>N}w dν_m=1 whenever m>N. This is a compact-space measure example, not a proposed genuine finite-energy NA output.

The additional zero-volume range actually proved is all actual numerically trivial rational bundles, including nontorsion Pic0 bundles, in the numerical varying-actual-bundle single-all-point-net cone convention. Its intrinsic reference is zero. Here is the proof, using only the actual ample G0 mathematical grant in its retained domain. Zero is genuine because L+εA is actual ample for each rational ε>0; the canonical weight-zero generating system gives the identically zero scalar, with numerical classes tending to zero. Constants are obtained by shifts. Conversely normalize u∈PSH(0) by u(v0)=sup u=0. Integer multiplication of its defining systems gives mu∈PSH(0) for every positive integer m. Tensor each incoming system into one fixed actual ample bundle once its actual ample difference is available; append low generator floors on a product net if finite stages are required. G0 thus puts every mu in the same normalized actual ample cone. At each fixed divisorial z, G0 normalized compactness gives a finite coordinate bound −C_z≤mu(z)≤0 independent of m. Hence u(z)=0. G0 all-point divisorial determination in that ample cone gives u=0 on the original carrier. Thus PSH(0)=R, without a nonample twice-closure assumption.

Positive ample perturbations have raw mass ε^n(A^n)→0. Every continuous test integral is bounded in absolute value by its sup norm times this mass, so their original-carrier limit is the zero measure. On constants their raw energies cε^n(A^n) tend to zero. Accordingly E1(0)=R, reference zero, raw energy zero and M0(c)=0. A positive Radon target of mass zero is necessarily the zero measure, of intrinsic dual energy zero. The zero equation is actually attained; every solution is a constant, hence unique modulo constants. Comparison and both zero derivatives are trivial. No probability normalization or division by zero is used.

This is not every zero-volume class. For L=p1*O(1) on P1×P1, L is nonzero nef of volume zero. Zero and a nonconstant bounded pullback FS scalar both have raw top measure zero, since adding εO(1,1) yields positive top products of mass 2ε(1+ε)→0. They are not equal modulo constants. This restricts the raw zero uniqueness claim; it is not a disproof of the desired positive-volume theorem.

Precise remaining obligations for the original full big domain are: independently complete/audit the genuine closure, envelope, compactness, section-energy and outer-output foundations in the unreviewed Complete151 body; prove nonalgebraic and negligible discrepancy nullness for every output, especially the reference and test section-envelope defects; prove all unbounded mixed moments and integration of every genuine E1 relative test without conditional defect assumptions; identify the genuine original-carrier weighted operator independently of every simultaneous unbounded approximation; construct fixed original continuous L1 approximants with uniform unbounded tails and collars selected before degree/measure limits; prove strong integration against every intrinsic finite-dual-energy target on weak cost-bounded sets; prove actual variational attainment without energy/integral jumps and only then use both derivative signs; prove all supporting planes, original Borel strict-set comparison, strict separation and uniqueness of every operator solution modulo constants.
